parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **production**?

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **fixed costs**?
choices: Costs that do not change when the level of output changes, such as rent
The amount by which total revenue exceeds total costs
Costs that change directly with the level of output, such as raw materials
The money received from selling output price multiplied by quantity sold

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (Costs that do not change when the level of output changes, such as rent)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of profit
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of variable costs
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of total revenue

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **variable costs**?
choices: The money received from selling output price multiplied by quantity sold
Costs that change directly with the level of output, such as raw materials
When total costs are greater than total revenue
The amount by which total revenue exceeds total costs

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (Costs that change directly with the level of output, such as raw materials)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of total revenue
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of loss
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of profit

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **total costs**?
choices: The cost per unit of output total costs divided by output
The sum of fixed costs and variable costs
The amount by which total revenue exceeds total costs
The money received from selling output price multiplied by quantity sold

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The sum of fixed costs and variable costs)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of average cost
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of profit
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of total revenue

Fatima runs a small printing shop in Porto. Monthly fixed costs are €4,000 and the business is considering buying a new machine that would double output but increase fixed costs.

The business sells about 4520 items a month at an average price of €4. Variable costs are about €1.80 per item. The new machine would cost €24,000 and raise fixed costs by €3,000 a month.

Fatima says orders have been turned away on busy days, but is unsure whether demand would be high enough to sell twice as much. The machine would also allow Fatima to cut the time staff spend on each item.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **profit maximisation**?
choices: When a firm grows by joining with another firm through a merger or takeover
When two firms at the same stage of production in the same industry join together
When two firms at different stages of production in the same industry join together
When a firm aims to produce at the output where the difference between total revenue and total costs is greatest

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (When a firm aims to produce at the output where the difference between total revenue and total costs is greatest)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of external growth
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of horizontal integration
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of vertical integration

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **organic growth**?
choices: When two firms agree to join together to form one firm
When two firms at the same stage of production in the same industry join together
When a firm grows internally by increasing output, for example opening new branches
When a firm aims to produce at the output where the difference between total revenue and total costs is greatest

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (When a firm grows internally by increasing output, for example opening new branches)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of merger
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of horizontal integration
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of profit maximisation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **external growth**?
choices: The percentage of total sales in a market made by one firm
When two firms at different stages of production in the same industry join together
When a firm grows by joining with another firm through a merger or takeover
When two firms at the same stage of production in the same industry join together

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (When a firm grows by joining with another firm through a merger or takeover)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of market share
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of vertical integration
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of horizontal integration

When a firm aims to produce at the output where the difference between total revenue and total costs is greatest

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of external growth
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of merger
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of profit maximisation

intro:
Redwood & Co is a family-owned hotel in Lisbon. The owners want to maximise profit, but the newly appointed managers want to increase market share and the firm's reputation for using sustainable materials.

Redwood & Co has 88 employees and made a profit of €3 million last year. Its market share is 9%. Sustainable materials cost about 11% more than standard materials.

A survey found that 40% of customers would pay more for sustainable products. The family owners rely on profits for their income and want to pay off a loan of €6 million within three years.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **economies of scale**?

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **monopoly**?
choices: A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent
A market with a single firm or one firm with a very large market share (over 25% in many legal definitions)
Competing using factors other than price such as branding, quality or advertising
A market with many firms none of which can control the market price

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A market with a single firm or one firm with a very large market share (over 25% in many legal definitions))
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of oligopoly
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-price competition
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of competitive market

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **oligopoly**?
choices: A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent
A firm that must accept the market price because it is too small to influence it
Factors that stop or discourage newcomers from starting to compete in an industry
When firms agree to work together for example to fix prices, rather than compete

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of price taker
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of barriers to entry
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of collusion

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **competitive market**?
choices: A market with a single firm or one firm with a very large market share (over 25% in many legal definitions)
A market with many firms none of which can control the market price
A firm that can set the price of its product because it has market power
Factors that stop or discourage newcomers from starting to compete in an industry

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A market with many firms none of which can control the market price)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of monopoly
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of price maker
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of barriers to entry

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **barriers to entry**?
choices: Factors that stop or discourage newcomers from starting to compete in an industry
A market with many firms none of which can control the market price
When firms agree to work together for example to fix prices, rather than compete
A market dominated by a few large firms that are interdependent

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (Factors that stop or discourage newcomers from starting to compete in an industry)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of competitive market
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of collusion
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of oligopoly

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **price maker**?

figures.label: Extract A
figures.text:
Software engineers in Leeds earn on average 2 times as much as shop assistants. Engineering firms report difficulty finding skilled staff, while many people apply for every shop job.

The average software engineer in Leeds earns £85,000 a year. There are about 5,000 unfilled software jobs. Engineering degrees take four years, and only 2,000 people graduate each year.

Online coding courses lasting a few months have become popular. Shop assistant jobs often need no qualifications, and many shops are introducing self-service tills. Some engineering firms are moving work to other countries where engineers are cheaper.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **privatisation**?
choices: The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the public sector to the private sector
The removal of rules and restrictions on firms in order to increase competition
Government action to prevent abuse of market power and promote competition between firms
Rules set by government or a regulator to control how firms behave

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the public sector to the private sector)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of competition policy
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of regulation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **nationalisation**?
choices: The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the public sector to the private sector
The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the private sector to the public sector/state
Rules set by government or a regulator to control how firms behave
A market where one firm can supply at a lower average cost than two or more firms could, such as water pipes

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The transfer of ownership of a firm or industry from the private sector to the public sector/state)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of privatisation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of regulation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of natural monopoly

rows.answer:

- Consumers are protected from high prices (1) because the water company is a monopoly (1), so the 2% cap stops it using its market power to raise bills sharply (1)

intro:
The government of Zentara has tried several times to privatise the main airport, but trade unions have opposed the sale. Private investors are now interested because passenger numbers are rising. Under state control, subsidies have paid for safety improvements and new facilities.

The airport handled 12 million passengers last year, up 8% on the year before. Government subsidies to the airport were Z£88 million. The airport has 3,000 workers, most of whom are union members.

Private investors say they would build a new terminal costing Z£537 million. In another country where an airport was privatised, landing charges for airlines rose by 24%, but waiting times at security fell.

intro:
The water industry in Ostrelia was privatised 20 years ago. Prices have risen faster than inflation and there are complaints about poor service. Some politicians want the industry to be nationalised.

Since privatisation, water prices have risen by 46%, while general prices rose by 36%. The companies paid O£2bn to shareholders last year. Investment in the network has risen, but 24% of customers say service is poor.

Nationalisation would cost the government an estimated O£17bn to buy the companies. Supporters say profits could be used to cut prices; critics point to long delays and losses when the industry was state-owned.
